subject: implementer
reason: Duplicate product entries are merged at the gRPC mapping boundary of Basket.API (BasketService.MapToCustomerBasket), so Redis stores one line per product with summed quantity and GetBasket/WebApp reflect it unchanged; single-entry updates keep their behavior and order, and identity/auth handling is untouched.

items.reason: Summing quantities with `existing.Quantity += item.Quantity` runs unchecked, so duplicate entries whose quantities add up past int.MaxValue wrap to a negative quantity that is stored. The gRPC path already lets a client store a negative quantity directly, so this is not a regression.
items.fix: Optionally sum in a `checked` context, or reject merged quantities outside a valid range (e.g. < 1) with RpcException(StatusCode.InvalidArgument), in line with BasketItem.Validate.

items.title: GetBasket after an update listing product 1 twice (1 + 2) returns one line with quantity 3
covers: Expected: The basket holds one line for product 1, with quantity 3
Expected: GetBasket returns that one line
items.reason: This is the bug as reported: two entries for product 1 were stored as two lines and `GetBasket` returned both. It reads back through `GetBasket` after the update so it proves what Redis holds, not only what the mapper returned. Functional (service over the real `RedisBasketRepository` and Redis) is the cheapest layer that includes persistence; a mocked repository would not show what is stored.

items.title: UpdateBasket response for product 1 listed twice (1 + 2) holds one line with quantity 3
covers: Expected: The basket holds one line for product 1, with quantity 3 (UpdateBasket's returned basket)
items.reason: `UpdateBasket` returns the stored basket, and callers (the WebApp's basket state) can use that response directly. If the merge happened only on read, or the response were built from the raw request, the caller would still see two lines. Separate from TC-BUG-33-01 because it checks a different output; functional so the response comes from the real repository round trip.

items.title: Product listed three times (1 + 1 + 1) is stored as one line with quantity 3
covers: Expected: one line, with the quantities of its entries added up
Bug report: a product listed more than once
items.reason: The bug says "more than once", not "twice": a fix that merged only the first pair would leave a second line for the third entry. Three entries of quantity 1 give the same total as the reported case, so the expected value is unambiguous. Functional for the same persistence reason as TC-BUG-33-01.

items.title: Duplicated product merges while another product listed once keeps its own line
covers: Expected: one line per product, quantities summed
Expected: Updates that list each product once behave as they do today
items.reason: A real basket mixes products. A merge keyed wrongly (for example collapsing all entries, or dropping the product between the duplicates) would corrupt the other line. This checks the duplicated product is summed and the product listed once is stored unchanged in the same update.

items.title: Update listing each product once stores one line per entry with the given quantities
covers: Expected: Updates that list each product once behave as they do today
items.reason: The story requires that the fix does not change ordinary updates. A regression here (quantities altered, lines dropped) would break every add-to-bag in the WebApp. Functional to confirm the round trip through Redis is unchanged.

items.title: A later update replaces the merged basket instead of adding to it
covers: Expected: quantities of its entries added up (entries of one update)
Expected: Updates that list each product once behave as they do today (update replaces the stored basket)
items.reason: The story sums the entries of one update; today an update replaces the whole stored basket. A fix that summed new entries into the stored lines would turn every quantity change in the WebApp into an increase. Functional because the risk only shows with a basket already stored in Redis.

items.title: Shopping bag shows product 1 once with quantity 3 and total $329.97 after a duplicate-entry update as bob
covers: Acceptance criteria: Given the test stack is running, When the steps are repeated, Then the result matches Expected
Expected: the shopping bag shows product 1 once, with quantity 3 and the matching total
items.reason: The acceptance criterion is the reproduction on the running test stack, ending in what `bob` sees in the shopping bag. Only e2e covers the real token, the deployed Basket.API, Redis and the WebApp rendering together. 109.99 × 3 = 329.97 is the "matching total".

items.title: UpdateBasket with product 1 listed twice and no authenticated user is refused with Unauthenticated and stores nothing
covers: Steps to Reproduce: step 1 (an access token for the caller is required)
Expected: Updates behave as they do today (anonymous UpdateBasket is refused)
items.reason: The reproduction starts from a token for `bob`, and the fix moves work into the mapping step that runs inside `UpdateBasket`. If the merge ran before the identity check, or a refactor dropped the check, an anonymous call could write a merged basket under an empty buyer id. Functional so the "stores nothing" half is checked against real Redis, not a mock.

items.title: Bob's update listing product 1 twice does not change another buyer's stored basket
covers: Expected: The basket holds one line for product 1 (the caller's basket only)
Expected: Updates behave as they do today (an update writes only the caller's basket)
items.reason: The merge must apply to the caller's basket only. A fix that merged into, or keyed lines across, stored baskets (for example by reading an existing basket by product instead of by buyer) would change alice's quantities when bob updates. Functional because the risk only shows with two baskets stored in the same real Redis.
